still_true: Wegovy's US list price is still $1,349 a month and still printed on the box. Almost nobody pays it.
The FDA has approved no generic semaglutide or tirzepatide in the US. Generic liraglutide is still the only generic incretin on the US market, and exclusivity still runs to roughly 2031–32.
The TrumpRx cash channel still operates, and oral Wegovy starting doses still cost $149 a month there.
The suicidal-ideation warning is still off the Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels, and the finalised 503B compounding exclusion still stands.

The September 2027 Labor/HHS/Treasury guidance is still federal policy: wellness programmes may tie up to a 30% premium differential to verified adherence or BMI, with a reasonable-alternative standard. Illinois's state ban, passed in 2028, still stands.

population.note: FICTIONAL estimates. Arithmetic: 28.5% ever-used − 21.3% current = 7.2% of adults (~19M) who have used the drugs and are off now. 44% of ever-users have cycled, which is ~12.5 points: ~10.6 points are current users on at least a second course (~50% of current users) and ~1.9 points are cyclers who are off again. That is consistent with roughly one-third persistence at a year and 36–47% restarting within a year over several cycles. The Medicare benefit pulled lapsed older users back in, which raised the restart share. 21.3% of ~267M adults ≈ 57M current users. Age check: adult shares of ~20/33/24/23% × 12/20/30/22% ≈ 21.3%. Payer mix (FICTIONAL, end-2030): Medicare 26% (~14.8M: ~12.6M aged, ~2.2M disabled), Medicaid 14% (~8.0M, ~5M of them under the new obesity indication), HRSA community programme 4% (~2.3M), commercial 26% (~14.8M), legitimate cash 20% (~11.4M), imported or counterfeit 10% (~5.7M). Public payers together cover 44%, the largest bloc, and ~55% of 2030 new starts. Obesity prevalence is ~33.6% (from 34.8%). About 21% of adults have obesity and have never used a drug, mostly uninsured working-age adults in the 9 states without Medicaid opt-in, people refusing on principle (the 'Whole Hunger' movement), and those excluded by BMI thresholds. The bottom-income figure rose most (11→18) because of Medicaid's enhanced match and the HRSA programme. Its gray-market dependence fell in share but grew in absolute numbers among people just above the HRSA income line. Under-18 use peaked at ~1.1% in late 2029 and fell to ~0.9% (~0.66M children) after the March 2030 growth communication. Under-12 starts fell by roughly half.

access.public_coverage: The Medicare and Medicaid Metabolic Health Act (enacted Jun 2029) added a Part D obesity benefit from 1 Jan 2030: BMI ≥30, or ≥27 with a comorbidity, prior authorisation, and reauthorisation at 12 months requiring ≥5% weight loss or a documented clinical reason. The manufacturer-agreed net price is ~$195/month across semaglutide, tirzepatide and orforglipron. Medicare arithmetic: ~14.8M users × $195 × 12 ≈ $34.6B annualised gross. About 8.5M of them would have been covered anyway under cardiovascular, CKD, sleep-apnoea, diabetes or dementia codes, so the incremental cost is ~6.3M × $195 × 12 ≈ $14.7B a year. Medicaid: a 90% federal match for obesity-indication fills. 41 states have opted in. ~5M obesity-indication users × $195 × 12 ≈ $11.7B, of which ~$10.5B is federal. CBO's 10-year score was ~$237B (2030–2039): Medicare ~$154B (assuming ~8M incremental users at an average net of ~$160 as prices step down: 8M × $160 × 12 × 10) plus Medicaid federal share ~$83B (~4.5M × $170 × 12 × 0.9 × 10), with no material offsets in the window. HRSA Community Metabolic Health programme (separate annual appropriation): free oral semaglutide through FQHCs for uninsured adults under 200% FPL, ~2.3M × $110 federal purchase price × 12 ≈ $3.0B a year. Typical Part D cost-sharing for an obesity fill is $25–60/month, under the annual out-of-pocket cap.
access.generic_rest_of_world: Indian generic semaglutide costs $5–35/month across 80+ brands. Canadian generics are CAD 60–95. Generics are sold in ~175 countries. Chinese makers now supply both generic semaglutide and unapproved 'research' retatrutide and tirzepatide peptides globally. India and China dominate volume outside the US.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Cash prices stepped down through negotiated channels. TrumpRx prices: Wegovy pill $149 for starting doses and $249 for maintenance (from $299). Foundayo $149–279. Injectable semaglutide and tirzepatide $299. Retatrutide (approved Mar 2029) $349. Oral amycretin, launched Oct 2030, $299 introductory. List prices are unchanged and unpaid. Orals are now ~64% of new starts and ~51% of all users. Employers covering weight management fell 44% → 41%, as some now let retirees and early-retiree cohorts move to Medicare. ~10% of employers cover only through monitored 'metabolic tracks', and enrolment is down from ~3M to ~2.4M after the California ban (2029) and EEOC technical assistance. The gray market grew from ~3M to ~5.7M users even as public coverage expanded. Growth came from people under BMI thresholds, people just above the HRSA income line, people avoiding adherence-monitored plans, young adults buying low doses for 'quiet mind' use, and 'reta' research-peptide buyers who want more than branded efficacy for less than $349. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak, and pressed counterfeit tablets are now part of the mix.

on_market_classes: GIP/GLP-1 dual agonist, weekly injectable (tirzepatide: Zepbound/Mounjaro)
GLP-1 agonist, daily oral peptide (Wegovy pill 25 mg; Rybelsus)
GLP-1/amylin unimolecular agonist, daily oral (amycretin oral, approved Sep 2030)
GIP/GLP-1/glucagon triple agonist, weekly injectable (retatrutide, approved Mar 2029)
GLP-1/glucagon dual agonist, weekly injectable (survodutide, Boehringer Ingelheim, approved Jul 2029, positioned for MASH)
GLP-1 agonist, daily injectable (liraglutide: Saxenda, incl. generics)
indications_beyond_weight_and_diabetes: adolescent obesity 12+ (semaglutide incl. Wegovy pill, liraglutide); growth-monitoring language added 2030
reduction of risk of all-cause dementia in adults with obesity and established CVD (tirzepatide; confirmatory trial ongoing)
alcohol use disorder, adults (Wegovy pill, Nov 2029)
aid to smoking and vaping cessation, including limiting post-cessation weight gain (Wegovy pill, Apr 2030)
mainstream_offlabel_uses: 'quiet mind' and 'focus' low-dose subscriptions from telehealth platforms, built on the AUD and cessation labels; the FDA has issued untitled letters but has not banned prescribing
dementia-prevention use by people without cardiovascular disease, cash-paid
microdosing for 'steadiness', now openly discussed as dose management rather than marketed by employers
gambling and compulsive-shopping reduction (observational support only)
planned 'drug holidays' on short-half-life Foundayo around weekends, holidays and anniversaries
drugs.pipeline_note: Oral parity, extended: the Wegovy pill matched injectable semaglutide in 2027. In Sep 2030 the FDA approved oral amycretin (Novo filed Mar 2029, ~18 months before approval) on phase 3 data showing ~19.8% mean weight loss at 68 weeks. That puts a pill in tirzepatide's cross-trial range for the first time. Lilly disputes the comparison, and a head-to-head against Zepbound reads out in 2031. Retatrutide was approved Mar 2029 at ~27% mean loss at the top dose, with dysesthesia in the warnings and slow titration. It is the efficacy ceiling, but persistence on it is lower. Survodutide was approved Jul 2029 and makes Boehringer the third US branded seller. Its uptake is mostly in hepatology. MariTide (monthly) was filed Jun 2030 and is not on the market. Bimagrumab-type muscle adjuncts have not been filed. The 'mood and motivation' driver is realised through approved addiction labels (AUD, nicotine) and the marketing built on them, not through any FDA mood indication. Novo's sNDA for binge-eating disorder was filed Oct 2030. Global incretin market ~$141B (2030). US net prices are falling ~6–8% a year through the Medicare and TrumpRx deals while US volume rises ~30%.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Retatrutide's top doses add more vomiting. Oral amycretin's early-titration nausea is comparable to Foundayo's.
Elevated with rapid weight loss; the absolute count is rising with the larger and older population.
Still no causal confirmation; absolute risk low.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; MDL settlements concluded 2029 without admission.

safety_ledger.effect: Lean mass (muscle) loss and bone-density loss
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: the 2029 extension of the Medicare cohort confirms a hip-fracture HR of ~1.3 after more than 2 years in users 65+. It is attenuated (HR ~1.15) among users with documented resistance training and protein counselling. Medicare's new obesity benefit has put ~4M more older adults on drug, so fracture counts are rising even as rates stabilise.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class warning (2028) retained. The Part D obesity benefit requires baseline DXA for beneficiaries 70+ and covers 6 physical-therapy strength sessions.
Listed as an adverse reaction; no class warning.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: No new signal in adults, including in the AUD and cessation trials.

safety_ledger.effect: Reward blunting / emotional flattening ('Ozempic personality', anhedonia)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: the FDA postmarketing study's 2030 interim (n≈61k) finds a clinically meaningful rise in ~8% of users versus ~3% of controls. It is dose-related, higher on retatrutide's top doses, and mostly reverses within 4–6 weeks of dose reduction. In surveys, ~38% of users report 'flatness' at some point and ~30% report a planned drug holiday in the past year.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: The FDA asked for labelling language on 'decreased interest or pleasure' in the AUD and cessation labels only (2030). The class label is under review.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Half to two-thirds regain within 18 months; worse after repeated cycles and disproportionately fat.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Used to justify the Medicare 12-month reauthorisation design and chronic-therapy framing.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Case series of B12, iron and vitamin D deficiency continue, concentrated in gray-market low-dose users and older Medicare starters.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: In professional guidance; the Medicare benefit's initial visit includes nutrition screening.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon effects beyond ~5 years of continuous use; effects in adolescents who may take these for decades; effects of repeated on/off cycling
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About eight years of follow-up exists. The pediatric growth signal (below) has made the adolescent question concrete.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric bone-density postmarketing requirement extended to all adolescent-labelled products.

safety_ledger.effect: Compounded / counterfeit / imported product harms (dosing errors, contamination)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: ~11,800 FDA adverse-event reports on non-approved product by mid-2030. The Aug 2029 counterfeit-pen cluster contained insulin and caused 212 severe hypoglycaemia cases and 7 deaths across 11 states. Pressed 'Wegovy pill' counterfeits contain no or variable drug. Mg/unit confusion persists. Research-grade 'reta' vials have no dose standard.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Expanded import alert. A CBP–India Post data-sharing agreement (2030). FDA pharmacy-verification campaign. Several states make sale of counterfeit incretins a felony. Personal-importation enforcement is still weak.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Reported in roughly 1 in 12 users at top doses; the leading specific reason for stopping retatrutide.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: In the Warnings section of the 2029 label, with titration guidance.

safety_ledger.effect: Growth, pubertal and eating-behaviour effects in children who started before 14
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: a US multisite pediatric network cohort (n≈41k adolescents with obesity, started at ages 10–13) found height velocity ~0.7 cm/year lower than matched non-users over 2 years, slower pubertal progression in boys, a BMD z-score accrual deficit of ~0.3, and new restrictive eating-disorder diagnoses (ARFID and anorexia-spectrum) at ~2.1% versus ~1.2% (HR ~1.7), mostly in girls. Endocrinologists note that obesity accelerates growth and puberty, so part of the slowing may be normalisation. Final adult height is unknown.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: FDA Drug Safety Communication (Mar 2030). Growth and pubertal monitoring every 3 months added to adolescent labels. EMA PRAC referral. AAP interim guidance: no use under 12 outside trials or specialist programmes, eating-disorder screening at every visit, and planned pauses considered during peak growth.

food_and_beverage.state: About 37% of US households have a user, and the Medicare benefit pushed the drug into older and rural households. Snack and confectionery volumes are ~8% below 2025 and sugary drinks ~7% below. Price, pack downsizing and protein lines keep dollar sales roughly flat to −2% in real terms. Grocery losses are now largest in small-town and rural Midwest and Southern stores, where older customers newly on Medicare shifted fastest. Independent bakeries and sourdough shops are growing in Whole Hunger cities like Boise and Nashville, a small countertrend. SNAP-heavy stores in HRSA-programme counties show the first snack-volume drop among low-income shoppers.

alcohol.state: After the AUD label (Nov 2029), primary-care and Medicaid prescribing for heavy drinking became routine. US spirits volumes are ~11% below 2025 and beer ~7%. Brown-Forman and Diageo have cut more US capacity, and no-alcohol and 'occasion' lines are the growth segment. Tobacco feels the cessation label: cigarette volume declines accelerated from ~9% to ~12% a year, and Altria and the vape makers are lobbying against Medicaid cessation coverage of the pill.

restaurants.state: Traffic is flat to slightly down. Checks are smaller, with small-plate, protein and 'half-portion' menus everywhere. Senior-heavy casual dining (Cracker Barrel, Golden Corral) saw a sharp per-cover drop after January 2030. Late-night bar hours keep shrinking in mid-sized cities. 'Hunger dinners' (long-table, unmedicated, prix fixe) are a small trendy format in Brooklyn, Nashville and Boise.

apparel.state: Plus-size specialists keep consolidating: Torrid is down about 45% in stores from 2024. Mainstream retailers manage a cycling customer with stretch, adjustable waistbands and resale. A small 'unmedicated' fashion niche sells soft tailoring as identity.

fitness.state: Strength training keeps growing. Medicare's PT strength sessions and the DXA requirement feed senior strength studios, and SilverSneakers-style programmes have moved to racks. Body-composition scanning chains are consolidating.

insurance.state: Commercial pharmacy trend eased to ~+6% as older and low-income users moved to public payers. Employer coverage is 41%. Monitored tracks are shrinking under the California ban and EEOC technical assistance requiring side-effect exemptions. Part D plans priced the obesity benefit into 2030–31 bids, and CMS is using premium-stabilisation funds. Medicaid budgets in non-opt-in states are under advocacy pressure. Actuaries are watching dementia and fracture claims move in opposite directions.

pharma.state: Volume is up sharply, and US net prices are down ~6–8% a year through Medicare and TrumpRx. Lilly leads on injectable efficacy with retatrutide. Novo regained momentum with the AUD and cessation labels and oral amycretin. Boehringer has entered through MASH. Telehealth platforms earn margin on 'quiet mind' subscriptions. Brand-protection and anti-counterfeit spend is a reported line item. Indian and Chinese generic makers dominate outside the US.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: Since Medicare and Medicaid began paying, a lean body signals less about money. The marker has moved to which drug and what muscle: retatrutide-lean, 'pill-lean' and 'Medicare-lean' (older, thinner, a little stooped) are distinguished in casual talk. A soft, full body on a young, well-dressed woman in Boise or Brooklyn increasingly reads as a choice: Whole Hunger.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The tiers have shifted rather than closed. Retirees and low-income adults in opt-in states now get branded pills through public payers. The squeezed tier is working-age people just above the HRSA line in the 9 non-opt-in states, who buy mail-order vials. The affluent buy efficacy (retatrutide, amycretin) and body-composition services, and increasingly pay to be seen not needing either. Upper-income parents are now the group most likely to pull children off the drug after the growth communication.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Meals are shorter and smaller, and 'food noise' is ordinary vocabulary. The Tulsa-born 'Bread Alone' fasting network claims ~1,100 congregations, many in rural Oklahoma, Texas and Arkansas. Whole Hunger hosts long-table 'hunger dinners' where guests declare themselves unmedicated. Holiday hosting guides now assume a third of guests are on a 'holiday' from the drug and will eat.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: Dating apps added an 'unmedicated' badge alongside 'on' and 'off'. In 2030 it is the fastest-growing badge among women 18–29 in Mountain West and Southern metros. 'Holiday-synced' couples, who stop the drug together for trips and anniversaries, are a recognised practice in couples therapy.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: The split hardened into identity. Institutions treat appetite as a health variable that public money now regulates. Whole Hunger treats it as evidence of being unmanaged and whole. The movement has an aesthetic (bread, butter, linen, visible softness, the open-hand logo) and a politics, opposing what it calls the 'Metabolic Health giveaway' to Lilly and Novo. It overlaps uneasily with MAHA state legislators, evangelical fasting groups, and the remnants of Brooklyn's Unmuted collective, which it partly absorbed.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL: the FDA PMR interim finds ~8% clinically meaningful anhedonia versus ~3% in controls, dose-related and largely reversible on dose reduction. About 38% of users report some 'flatness' in surveys, and ~30% took a planned drug holiday in the past year. Holidays are easiest on Foundayo, whose roughly day-and-a-half half-life lets a weekend off take effect. On weekly semaglutide or the long-half-life Wegovy pill, a 'holiday' takes 1–2 weeks to be felt, which is why forums trade Foundayo switching advice.
interior_life.framing: Mostly a side effect people manage, called 'the flats'. The fixes are 'dosing down', 'Foundayo weekends' and 'holidays'. Telehealth still markets the same effect as 'quiet mind', and employers have quietly dropped 'steadiness' from HR decks after the EEOC guidance and a 2029 class settlement. Whole Hunger calls it sedation. Clinicians increasingly ask about it at refill visits.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Adherence-verified tracks cover ~2.4M employees, down from ~3M. The EEOC's 2029 technical assistance says differentials must exempt people who reduce or stop doses for documented side effects including mood flattening, so 'dose-flex' clauses are now standard. Managers talk openly about the flats in performance reviews, and 'on holiday' is a recognised explanation for a bad week, a good pitch, or both. Sales and creative firms are informally sceptical of hires who are 'too steady'.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Flat fiction' has passed into parody. The new genre is 'holiday' work: albums, stand-up sets and gallery nights explicitly made off-dose. Sportsbooks and casinos price in lower wagering and market to 'holiday weekends'. Late-night culture in mid-sized cities is thinner but spikes around long weekends.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Desire mismatch remains the leading presenting issue tied to the drugs. Planned holidays around anniversaries, holidays and conception attempts are common, which keeps the cycling rate high. Therapists report couples arguing over whether a partner is 'themselves' on or off.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: Mood marketing reached Congress. A Senate HELP hearing (2030) on 'quiet mind' telehealth ads produced FDA untitled letters but no statute. The subsidy law split both parties: Whole Hunger and some MAHA-aligned governors campaign against Medicaid opt-in, while senior groups defend the Part D benefit. California's adherence-premium ban passed in 2029, and New York's is pending. Still no measurable turnout effect.

state.regulatory_posture: Fast on adult approvals (retatrutide, survodutide, oral amycretin, the AUD and cessation labels) and newly cautious on children after the March 2030 Drug Safety Communication. Enforcement against counterfeits is tougher on paper and still porous at the mailbox. Promotional enforcement against 'quiet mind' telehealth is limited to untitled letters.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate. Direct subsidy has become policy. The Medicare and Medicaid Metabolic Health Act (Jun 2029) created the Part D obesity benefit from Jan 2030 at a ~$195 net negotiated price, and a 90% federal Medicaid match taken up by 41 states. The HRSA Community Metabolic Health programme (from Oct 2029) gives free oral semaglutide at FQHCs to uninsured adults under 200% FPL, ~2.3M users at ~$3.0B a year. Medicaid and HRSA also cover the Wegovy pill for cessation.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Public coverage has its own condition: Medicare and most Medicaid programmes reauthorise at 12 months on ≥5% weight loss or a documented reason, and Medicaid states may require 6-month check-ins. PBM fill data and app logs still feed employer wellness vendors under consent. Fill-based adherence cannot see daily ingestion, so 'holiday' users stay compliant on paper. Federal guidance allowing 30% differentials stands. Illinois and California ban them.
state.workforce_or_military: TRICARE matched the Medicare obesity criteria in 2030. The Army's supervised oral pilot for near-standard recruits has been made permanent and expanded to the Navy. DOT issued guidance (2029) allowing incretin use by commercial drivers with no medical-certification restriction, while warning on hypoglycaemia risk from non-FDA product.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: India and China supply most of the world's semaglutide and the gray-market US supply. The 2030 US–India trade framework includes CBP–India Post data sharing and Indian export checks on unlabelled peptide shipments. Chinese 'research peptide' exporters are a new irritant in US–China talks. Lilly and Novo traded the $195 Medicare price for tariff relief on imported API and onshoring commitments in North Carolina and Indiana.

events.event: FDA approves Lilly's retatrutide for chronic weight management with a dysesthesia warning; at ~27% mean loss it becomes the efficacy ceiling, and research-grade 'reta' vials from Chinese sellers had already been circulating for a year

Congress passes the Medicare and Medicaid Metabolic Health Act after Lilly and Novo agree to a ~$195 net price in exchange for tariff relief; CBO scores it at ~$237B over ten years; the Part D obesity benefit starts 1 January 2030 and 41 states take the 90% Medicaid match by year-end

CDC and FDA link counterfeit 'semaglutide' pens containing insulin to 212 severe hypoglycaemia cases and 7 deaths in 11 states; pressed counterfeit Wegovy tablets are found in mail seizures; the HRSA free-pill programme launches in October, pitched partly as a counterfeit countermeasure

FDA Drug Safety Communication on slower growth, delayed puberty and restrictive eating disorders in children who started incretins before 14; AAP advises against use under 12 outside trials; pediatric starts fall by about a third within months

FDA approves the Wegovy pill as an aid to smoking and vaping cessation, five months after its alcohol-use-disorder approval; telehealth platforms launch low-dose 'quiet mind' subscriptions within weeks, and the FDA answers with untitled letters

FDA approves Novo's oral amycretin at ~19.8% mean weight loss, the first pill in tirzepatide's range; TrumpRx lists it at $299 and Lilly disputes the cross-trial comparison ahead of a 2031 head-to-head

open_tensions: Medicare is now the default payer for older users. That puts millions more 70-year-olds on drugs carrying a bone and fracture warning, against a contested dementia benefit, with fracture claims and CBO's ~$237B score likely to collide in the 2031 Part D bids.

Public coverage expanded while the gray market nearly doubled to ~5.7M users. The people just above the HRSA line, in non-opt-in states, or chasing retatrutide-level results get counterfeit pens and research peptides, and the insulin-pen deaths did not stop the mail.

The pediatric growth signal is real but confounded. Final adult height and peak bone mass will not be known for years, while ~0.66M children stay on drug and parents, AAP and the FDA disagree on pauses during peak growth.

Reward blunting is now a mainstream complaint, managed with holidays that fill data can't see. Telehealth sells the same effect as 'quiet mind', employers can still tie 30% of premiums to adherence outside Illinois and California, and Whole Hunger is turning refusal into a voting bloc against the subsidy.

prose.headline: One in Five, on the Government's Tab: Medicare pays, the pill matches the pen, and pediatricians are measuring children again
prose.world_in_600_words:
At the end of 2030 one American adult in five takes an incretin drug, and most of them swallow it. The needle is now a minority habit. Two years ago a daily semaglutide pill caught up with the weekly pen. This September a pill from Novo, oral amycretin, posted results in the range that only Lilly's injectables used to reach. Lilly's answer, retatrutide, takes off more weight than anything else on the market and makes about one top-dose user in twelve feel their skin as if it were sunburnt.

The bigger change is who pays. In June 2029 Congress did what it had refused to do eighteen months earlier, when it let the Medicare pilot die over a forty-one-billion-dollar score. It passed a far larger obesity benefit. The difference was the election, a visible cohort of regaining retirees, and a deal in which Lilly and Novo accepted about $195 a month from public payers in exchange for tariff relief. Since January, Medicare covers the drugs for obesity behind prior authorisation, with a twelve-month check on whether they are working. Forty-one states have taken a ninety-percent federal match for Medicaid. Community health centres hand out free pills to uninsured adults near the poverty line. Public programmes now pay for more of these drugs than employers do. List prices still sit on boxes nobody reads, and cash prices on the government's site have stepped down to the low hundreds.

Public money has not emptied the mail. The gray market nearly doubled, to almost six million people. They fall in the gaps: earning a little too much for the free programme, living in one of the nine states that declined the match, or wanting what retatrutide does for less than retatrutide costs. Last August counterfeit pens filled with insulin sent two hundred people into hypoglycaemic crisis and killed seven. Pressed fake pills followed. Enforcement now has a data-sharing deal with India's postal service, and the packages still arrive.

The drugs gained two new kinds of labels: alcohol-use disorder and quitting cigarettes and vapes. Cigarette sales are falling faster, and so are spirits. Telehealth companies took the same mechanism and sold it as 'quiet mind', a low-dose subscription for people who want less craving of every kind. The FDA has sent letters. People talk about the flatness now in ordinary terms: the flats, dosing down, a holiday. Foundayo clears the body fast enough that a weekend off is felt, so it has become the pill of people who want their Saturdays back. Pharmacy fill records cannot tell, so the employers still tying premiums to adherence mostly see compliance. California has banned those premiums. The federal rule allowing them stands.

In March the FDA told parents that children who started before fourteen were growing more slowly, maturing later, and developing restrictive eating disorders more often than matched children who didn't take the drugs. Endocrinologists point out that obesity speeds growth, so some of the slowing may be a correction. Nobody yet knows how tall these children will end up. Pediatric starts fell by a third, mostly in the affluent families who had started them first.

Against all this a movement has grown that calls itself Whole Hunger. It is young, mostly female, strongest in Boise, Nashville and Brooklyn, and attached to bread, linen and softness worn as a choice. It eats at long tables and campaigns against Medicaid opt-in alongside rural fasting congregations and MAHA-aligned governors who distrust the deal. Snack makers sell smaller bags in rural Midwest groceries, where the newly covered retirees changed their carts. Senior strength studios are full. Obesity is falling. Most numbers look better than they did, which is why the arguments are about the ones that don't.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Marisol Vega takes her Foundayo at 6:10 on Friday, standing at the counter in Columbus, and taps the app. Tomorrow she won't take one, and she won't tap. On Monday the app will still show a full week. Her claims-processing job counts refills, not mornings.

At work Dee from the next pod asks whether she's 'going on holiday' this weekend. Marisol says maybe. Her sister's wedding is Saturday and she would like to want the cake.

At three she leaves early for Nationwide Children's. Ari is thirteen and has been on the Wegovy pill since a month before he turned twelve. A nurse stands him against the wall, taps the bar onto his hair, and reads the number twice. The endocrinologist turns the screen so Marisol can see the line. It is still going up. It used to be steeper.

'Some of that is just him normalising,' the doctor says. 'Some of it we don't know.' She suggests stopping over the summer, which is when boys his age often shoot up, and checking again in September. Ari says nothing about the summer. He asks whether he'll get hungry again. The doctor says probably.

On the drive home they pass the new bakery on High Street. Its window says WHOLE HUNGER in flour-white paint, and a line of women in loose linen waits outside. Ari watches them.

Her father calls from Toledo. Medicare approved his pill, thirty-five dollars, and they want a bone scan first. He sounds pleased about the scan.

On Saturday morning Marisol leaves the bottle in the cabinet and makes pancakes. Ari eats two, slowly, then a third.
